description: Structured summary of real (--provider claude, unless noted) executions of authored routing/behavior Eval cases against a live model, one row per case attempt. This is a SUMMARY ledger (skill, case id, kind, result) for Bayesian/priority-ranking analysis tools -- it intentionally does NOT include prompts or full model output; raw JSONL evidence for each entry lives locally under evals/runtime/results/ (gitignored, machine-local, not committed) and is cited here by filename only. Append-only: add new rows for new executions, never edit or delete an existing row's outcome after the fact -- a re-grade or correction gets a new row with a note, mirroring lifecycle.json's own append-only notes discipline.

result_values.PASS: content and routing both matched the case's contract cleanly
result_values.PASS_DEVIATION_ROUTING: content fully satisfied required/forbidden behaviors, but a different primary_skill was selected than the skill under test and no expected_alternative_skill was declared
result_values.PASS_DEVIATION_MINOR: primary skill matched but an unrequired-but-not-forbidden supporting skill was also selected (weaker model only, e.g. ollama)
result_values.FAIL_CONTENT: primary skill matched (or deviation still graded on content) but the actual output failed to satisfy one or more required_behaviors, or triggered a forbidden_behavior
result_values.FAIL_ROUTING: primary_skill=None or otherwise no skill selected despite expected_routing=true, so no behavior content was produced to grade
result_values.BLOCKED_HARNESS: the case cannot be executed by the current 2-stage harness at all (not a model-quality result) -- e.g. the model correctly selected using-cloudbox-skills itself as primary_skill, but the harness's selected-skills stage 2 hard-refuses to load using-cloudbox-skills as a downstream skill; excluded from priority-ranker PASS/FAIL statistics until the harness gains a self-referential-router execution path

application case (executive/engineering views from one field-update evidence set, preserving statistical scope): routing stage itself was on-target (primary_skill=document-governance, supporting_skills=['software-quality-iso25010'], execution_order correctly document-governance-first) but the model hallucinated a non-existent skill ID 'software-quality-iso25010-as-primary' inside rejected_skills; the harness's deterministic contract_repair flagged it as an unknown-skill-ID schema error but could not fix it, and the 2-stage harness refuses to run stage 2 (the actual behavior deliverable) when the routing decision is contract-invalid, even though the invalid field (rejected_skills) is not one this case's own grading criteria depend on. This is a genuine, repeatable harness defect (see also DOC-BEH-011 below), not a document-governance content or routing defect -- worth fixing either by having contract_repair drop/ignore unknown IDs found only in rejected_skills, or by relaxing the stage-2 gate to depend only on primary_skill/supporting_skills validity.

discipline case (publishing a deliberately terminal status-only commit to a downstream/mirror-only copy, intended never to be merged back): routing deviated to coding-agent-git-discipline (undeclared, expected_alternative_skill was null). The resulting deliverable is a thorough, safe git-mechanics procedure (auth handling, message integrity, remote read-back, branch protection) but never performs the document-governance-specific check this case exists to test: confirming whether the downstream copy will genuinely receive no further legitimate sync BEFORE isolating the commit there. It takes the terminal/isolated intent as a given rather than verifying it, and the whole procedure isolates the commit on the mirror without checking future sync need -- this is exactly forbidden_behavior #1 ('isolating a status commit on a downstream remote without checking whether that remote will need a real content sync later'), and required_behaviors #1/#2 (confirm-before-isolating; land upstream instead when sync is plausible) are both unmet. Graded FAIL_CONTENT. Real finding: when this prompt routes to the git-mechanics skill instead of document-governance, the governance-level permanence judgment this case is designed to exercise is lost entirely -- worth a cross-reference from coding-agent-git-discipline to this document-governance case/rule, or a routing-reference nudge, as a follow-up.

This is exactly the generalization DOC-BEH-008 was authored to test (per its own review_notes, distilled 2026-08-23 specifically to confirm the conflicting-source-data discipline extends beyond engineering/equipment documents to personal/career documents) -- the live router does not yet make this scope extension visible enough to select document-governance for a personal-document prompt. No behavior_output was produced (primary_skill=None), so none of the 3 required_behaviors could be checked against real content. Graded FAIL_ROUTING per the grading-rules definition. Real, repeatable routing gap worth a SKILL.md/routing-reference fix: document-governance's own trigger description should explicitly mention personal/career documents, not only engineering ones, to close this gap.
